html:
SMTO-EXE-0036 — Too much text was sent into one command

GUID: ff940069-6c77-42ef-96fd-b7c75eb461d2
Slug: shell-stdin-limit
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to feed more than about 1 MB of text straight into a command, which is over its limit. The command did not run and nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to save the data to a file first and then have the command open that file. A command can read a large file, but it can't take that much text passed in directly.
  2. If a file won't work for this command, ask SMTO to split the data into smaller parts and handle them one at a time. Each smaller part stays under the size SMTO can pass straight into a command.
  3. Check that the result covers all of your data, not just the first part. Cutting the data short would make the command work with incomplete information.

What success looks like

  • The step runs and its output covers all of the data you meant to process.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete earlier results or trim the data just to make it fit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The prepared shell stdin (literal or from a bound input) exceeded the 1,048,576-character limit, so the command was rejected before launch.

What this means

  • The prepared shell stdin byte buffer exceeded 1,048,576 bytes after literal or bound-input conversion. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The prepared shell stdin byte buffer exceeded 1,048,576 bytes after literal or bound-input conversion.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure the encoded stdin size and inspect available artifact/file input support for the intended command.

How to fix it

  • Write the complete input to a file or artifact and have the command read it by path, or split the input across several commands (agent_runtime.execution.shell_request.prepare_request enforces the 1 MiB stdin limit). Do not truncate the input or delete stored receipts to fit.
  • Store the complete input as an artifact and pass its supported reference instead of truncating stdin.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete input reaches the command through a supported bounded channel without truncation.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
